conventions.geometry: Oriented finite-type hyperbolic curvature -1, no cone singularities. Each theorem adds its own compactness, cusp and boundary hypotheses.
conventions.curves: Unoriented free-homotopy classes by default. Figure-eights are primitive one-transverse-double-point classes; the torus contributes two N labels and one H label per simple alpha. Equal lengths do not identify labels.
conventions.traces: Positive geometric t=2cosh(ell/2), cusp t=2. Pants lifts trA=t_a, trB=t_b, trAB=-t_c; cusp parabolic factorization instead trA=t_a,trB=-t_b,AB=P. These are local compatible signs, not a universal positive SL(2) lift. Section 23 retains signed characters.
conventions.twists: Signed hyperbolic displacement with Dehn-twist period a>0. Angles and endpoint tangential coordinates use the compatible signed convention. Fixed curve length is not periodic; its orbit sum is.
conventions.endpoint_phase: Orient by travel, p in (-1,1); dL=-p_s ds+p_t dt. Common cuff coordinate after reversal of one induced boundary orientation; opposite-side crossing plus equal p matches the full unit tangent.
conventions.branches: acosh nonnegative real branch on [1,infinity); all displayed square roots nonnegative; invalid domains are not clamped.
conventions.cusps: lambda=exp(signed truncated distance/2), without sqrt(2). H denotes an embedded sufficiently small horocycle for literal truncation, or a positive decoration with signed length when larger. Gap partition assumes no geodesic boundary.
conventions.basmajian: Oriented orthogeodesics contribute 2log(coth(d/2)); grouping reverse orientations gives 4 for one unoriented arc. The boundary spectrum includes nonsimple arcs.
conventions.WP: Same orbifold measure on both unfolded quotients. Punctured-torus stack measure includes one ineffective factor 1/2, consistent with reviewed Section 6.
conventions.numerics: Author finite checks use exact SymPy identities and mpmath at 70/110 digits. Floating residuals are not intervals. Analytic truncation bounds are separate from quadrature/roundoff; tiny positive signals use stable or scaled forms.
